The games serve as a significant learning experience for India, especially with the country set to host the event in 2030.

Sports.headline: Shah Rukh Khan celebrates LA Knight Riders' maiden MLC title after thrilling final win
Sports.summary: Shah Rukh Khan, co-owner of the Kolkata Knight Riders franchise, celebrated the LA Knight Riders' first Major League Cricket (MLC) title victory. The team secured a thrilling one-run win over Washington Freedom in the final. This win marks a significant achievement for the Knight Riders brand in the growing US cricket league.

Science.headline: Gaia Sausage collision may have flipped the Milky Way by 90° 10 billion years ago
Science.summary: Astronomers suggest that a dramatic collision between the Milky Way and a dwarf galaxy, dubbed the "Gaia Sausage," approximately 10 billion years ago may have flipped our galaxy's orientation by over 90 degrees. Researchers from Durham University propose this cosmic event occurred long before our solar system formed. This finding offers new insights into the Milky Way's ancient and violent history.

The event happened before our solar system existed.

Science.headline: Scientists found a 2,865-pound predator from before dinosaurs ruled Earth
Science.summary: Scientists have discovered the remains of a 2,865-pound predator that roamed Earth millions of years before dinosaurs became dominant. This massive ancient creature provides new insights into prehistoric ecosystems and the evolutionary paths of early apex predators. The discovery helps to paint a more complete picture of life during the pre-dinosaur era.

Science.headline: Beavers do more than build dams, they create wetlands, raise groundwater, and lock away carbon
Science.summary: Beavers, weighing around 20 kilograms, are revealed to be significant ecosystem engineers, doing much more than just building dams. These rodents create vital wetlands, help raise groundwater levels, and play a crucial role in carbon sequestration. Their activities contribute significantly to biodiversity and environmental health.

Science.headline: 24-million-year-old Kevda fossil leaves discovered in Assam reveal ancient tropical forests of India
Science.summary: Scientists have discovered 24-million-year-old Kevda fossil leaves in Assam, providing crucial evidence of ancient tropical forests in India. This finding offers insights into India's paleoenvironment and climate history, suggesting a significantly different flora composition millions of years ago. The discovery enriches our understanding of biodiversity evolution in the region.

Science.headline: International Space Station’s $23 million toilet recycles 98% of water into drinking water
Science.summary: The International Space Station's $23 million toilet is far more than a waste disposal unit; it plays a critical role in the station's life support system. This advanced facility recycles approximately 98% of the station's water, including urine and humidity, transforming it into potable drinking water for astronauts. Its efficiency is vital for long-duration space missions, minimizing the need for resupply.

Health.headline: Healthy couples can still carry hidden blood disorder genes: Why early screening matters
Health.summary: Even outwardly healthy couples can unknowingly carry hidden genes for blood disorders, making early genetic screening crucial before starting a family. Such screenings can identify risks for conditions like thalassemia or sickle cell anemia, allowing couples to make informed decisions and seek appropriate medical guidance. This proactive approach can significantly impact the health of future generations.

Early genetic screening is vital before starting a family.

Allows informed decisions and medical guidance for prospective parents.

Health.headline: Why waist-to-height ratio beats BMI in predicting heart disease and diabetes
Health.summary: Research suggests that the waist-to-height ratio is a more accurate predictor of heart disease and diabetes risk than the traditional Body Mass Index (BMI). This alternative measure specifically addresses central obesity, which is strongly linked to cardiometabolic diseases. Although India's health ministry directive on waist-to-hip ratio might face cultural resistance, better measures are available for identifying at-risk individuals.

It specifically targets central obesity, a key risk factor.
This measure could offer more precise risk assessment.
India's health ministry's directive on waist-to-hip ratio may face cultural hurdles.

Health.summary: The US has issued a travel advisory due to a chikungunya outbreak, detailing affected countries, symptoms to watch for, and protective measures for travelers. Health.summary: Europe's health agency has reported a concerning rise in antibiotic-resistant gonorrhea cases across the continent. This trend poses a significant public health challenge, as treatment options become increasingly limited, raising the specter of untreatable infections. Public health officials are urging increased surveillance and responsible antibiotic use to combat the spread.
